messages:
mike-ops: Heads up — ap-southeast-2 queue depth spiked for mosaic-13b-qa, per-model backlog up ~3.2x over baseline, GPU p99 utilization > 92% :warning:
monitor-bot: ALERT ap-se2: queue_depth(mosaic-13b-qa) = 1200 (baseline 370) | p99_gpu_util=92.8% | avg_latency=1.6s
anya-platform: Wow. Any single-tenant causing it or broad?
kai-infra: Seeing a handful of large batched jobs from acct:nomad-ads (bursty evals) + some sustained traffic from acme-proxy. Admission controller logs show many requests hitting admission:requeue at the scheduling layer.
jess-sre: Can we verify whether prefix/KV caching is effective? If KV miss rate high, model runs will be heavier.
mike-ops: Checked KV hit — ~78% for this model (normal). This looks capacity-driven, not cache miss.
anya-platform: Two quick levers: 1) soft-throttle low-priority routes for mosaic-13b-qa 2) route nomad-ads to quantized variant mosaic-13b-q4 if acceptable. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
kai-infra: Agreed. Also consider lowering per-request token cap for non-SLA tenants to reduce worst-case sequences.
ops-bot: Proposed config diff applied to staging admission controller: ```yaml
admission:
  default: {concurrency: 1000}
  per_model:
    mosaic-13b-qa: {max_inflight: 300, priority: high}
    mosaic-13b-q4: {max_inflight: 120, priority: medium}
  tenant_overrides:
    nomad-ads: {priority: low, token_cap: 512}
```
ops-bot: (staging) tests passed, will push to canary in 2m
mike-ops: Rolling canary now in ap-se2 for admission change. Monitoring queue depth and drop rates. :eyes:
monitor-bot: CANARY: applied admission diff to 10% of ap-se2 pods
jess-sre: Also flip on fairshare spillover to us-west as fallback for low-latency tolerant tenants. We should avoid sending high-priority traffic.
anya-platform: Important: traffic shaping to other regions will incur egress cost and higher latency — add cost note to the change.
kai-infra: On scaling side, we have one maintenance GPU pool freeing in ~28m (aps1 drift); we could temporarily add 6 p3-equivalent slots to ap-se2 via burst capacity. Ops cost estimate ~ $180/hr.
mike-ops: I'd rather avoid spend if config changes buy time. Plan: 1) enable admission diff (in canary) 2) schedule tenant reroute for nomad-ads to q4 3) prepare rapid-burst plan if queue depth doesn't drop in 20m.
anya-platform: Who owns doing the reroute config? Kai?
kai-infra: I can push tenant policy to re-route nomad-ads to mosaic-13b-q4 (nonbreaking). Doing it now.
ops-bot: tenant policy update queued: nomad-ads -> mosaic-13b-q4 (gradual 5% -> 100% over 5m)
monitor-bot: 5m checkset scheduled.
jess-sre: Also adding short-term token-based soft limits for anonymous/free tiers: `rate_limit: 10r/s` per token to reduce noisy low-value traffic.
mike-ops: Thanks. If after 20m we still see >2x baseline queue, we'll open the burst plan and notify billing to confirm spend ok.
anya-platform: Please add a short note in the runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/queue-triage with the decision and cost delta.
kai-infra: Added runbook entry and pinned the config diff.
monitor-bot: METRIC_UPDATE (10m): queue_depth(mosaic-13b-qa) reduced from 1200 -> 510, p99_gpu_util -> 86.4%
jess-sre: Nice, that's trending down. Keep an eye on tail latencies — soft-throttle may push retries.
mike-ops: Will watch tail and error budget. If retries spike, we may need to loosen token caps for high-SLA tenants.
anya-platform: Postmortem owner? I'll take lead if this becomes a sustained pattern.
mike-ops: Thanks. Actions assigned: kara to monitor (mike-ops), kai to adjust tenant policy, jess to watch SLOs, anya to do follow-up PM note.
anya-platform: TL;DR: admission control + tenant reroute reduced queue by ~58% without burst spend. Reopen if backlog returns. :thumbsup:
